_comment: Authorities the evaluate and gap-check steps may cite. `verify: true` marks a citation that still needs a human check against the current source. Summaries are working notes for a reviewer, not quotations.

authorities.title: Normal knee range of motion
authorities.summary: Normal knee motion is flexion to 140° and extension to 0°.

authorities.title: Zero percent evaluations
authorities.summary: Where the schedule does not provide a 0% evaluation, 0% is assigned when the requirements for a compensable evaluation are not met.

authorities.title: Higher of two evaluations
authorities.summary: Where there is a question as to which of two evaluations applies, the higher is assigned if the disability picture more nearly approximates its criteria; otherwise the lower.

authorities.title: Functional loss
authorities.summary: Functional loss may be due to pain, supported by adequate pathology and evidenced by visible behavior on motion; weakness is as important as limitation of motion.

authorities.title: The joints
authorities.summary: Factors of disability of the joints: less movement than normal, more movement than normal, weakened movement, excess fatigability, incoordination, pain on movement, swelling, deformity, atrophy.

authorities.title: Painful motion
authorities.summary: Painful motion is entitled to at least the minimum compensable rating for the joint; the joint should be tested for pain on both active and passive motion, in weight-bearing and nonweight-bearing, and if possible with the range of the opposite undamaged joint.

authorities.title: Combined ratings table
authorities.summary: Separate ratings are combined, not added, under the combined ratings table.

authorities.title: Arthritis, degenerative
authorities.summary: Degenerative arthritis established by imaging is rated on limitation of motion of the affected joint; where noncompensable, 10% for each major joint or group affected by limitation of motion, objectively confirmed.

authorities.title: Knee, other impairment of (instability / subluxation)
authorities.summary: Separate rating for recurrent subluxation or lateral instability. Criteria were revised effective 2021-02-07; not modeled in this slice.

authorities.title: Functional loss on repetitive use and flare-ups
authorities.summary: Ratings based on limitation of motion must consider functional loss due to pain, weakness, fatigability and incoordination under §§ 4.40 and 4.45, including on repeated use and during flare-ups; the examiner should express additional loss in degrees where possible.

authorities.title: Pain must produce functional loss
authorities.summary: Pain alone does not equal limitation of motion; the examiner must address whether pain causes functional loss and, if so, its extent.

authorities.title: § 4.59 testing requirements
authorities.summary: An examination that fails to test for pain on active and passive motion, in weight-bearing and nonweight-bearing, and (if possible) the opposite undamaged joint, is inadequate for rating purposes unless the examiner explains why such testing could not be done.

authorities.title: Flare-up estimates
authorities.summary: The examiner must elicit relevant information about flare-ups (frequency, duration, characteristics, severity, functional loss) and estimate functional loss during flares, or explain why an estimate cannot be given; an exam is not inadequate merely because it was not conducted during a flare.

authorities.title: Refusal to estimate flare-up loss
authorities.summary: An examiner may not decline to estimate flare-up functional loss solely because the veteran was not examined during a flare-up.

authorities.title: § 4.59 minimum rating regardless of arthritis
authorities.summary: § 4.59 provides for at least the minimum compensable rating for an actually painful joint whether or not arthritis is present.

authorities.title: § 4.59 not limited to ROM-based codes
authorities.summary: § 4.59 applies to painful joints regardless of whether the diagnostic code is predicated on range of motion.

authorities.title: Probative value of a medical opinion
authorities.summary: A medical opinion's probative value depends on whether it is based on accurate facts and supported by a reasoned analysis; a bare conclusion is inadequate.

authorities.title: Adequate medical opinion
authorities.summary: An adequate opinion must support its conclusion with an analysis the Board can weigh against contrary opinions.

authorities.title: Speculation opinions
authorities.summary: An opinion that a matter cannot be resolved without resort to speculation is adequate only if the examiner explains why, after considering all procurable information.

authorities.title: Duty to ensure an adequate examination
authorities.summary: Once VA undertakes to provide an examination, it must ensure the examination is adequate.

authorities.title: Separate knee ratings (meniscal, instability, ROM)
authorities.summary: Evaluation under DC 5257 or 5261 does not by itself preclude a separate rating under DC 5258 or 5259 for meniscal symptoms not compensated by the other code.

authorities.title: Separate ratings for flexion and extension of the same knee
authorities.summary: A veteran may receive separate ratings under DC 5260 and DC 5261 for limitation of flexion and limitation of extension of the same joint.

authorities.title: Arthritis and instability of the knee
authorities.summary: Separate ratings may be assigned for arthritis with limitation of motion and for instability of the same knee under DC 5257.

authorities.title: Arthritis and instability of the knee (clarification)
authorities.summary: Clarifies 23-97: a separate arthritis rating with DC 5257 requires limitation of motion that is at least noncompensable under DC 5260/5261 or painful motion under § 4.59.

authorities.title: Adjudication manual — musculoskeletal rating procedures
authorities.summary: Rating procedures for musculoskeletal conditions, including use of DBQ range-of-motion findings. Section numbering changes with manual reorganizations; verify the current citation before relying on it.
